​Functions of the Assessor’s Office
The county assessor has the duty to value all real and personal property in the county as a basis for the governing boards of various governmental subdivisions (counties, schools, villages, cities, natural resources districts, community colleges, educational service units) to levy taxes. The assessor must be certified by the Department of Revenue, division of Property Assessment in order to run for and to hold office, and must annually attend training sessions to obtain the required continuing education hours to be re-certified. Other duties of the office of county assessor include: Physically inspect each parcel in the county (over 10,000) at least once every six years;
Establish and maintain fair and equitable value on all rea land personal property withing he county;
Attend all meetings of the County Board of Equalization;
Review all applications for religious, charitable and educational tax exemptions;
Accept and process homestead exemption applications;
Accept and process personal property schedules;
Verity and maintain a sales file for all property within the county;
Respond to request for information from the public.
